column1: # What Elenchus refuses, enforced rather than written down.
# Every row here was already doctrine in CLAUDE.md and enforced by nothing. The
# gate row is the one that has actually cost something: an untracked, day-stale
# copy of the gate at scripts/gate.sh runs seven checks against the eight Felix
# runs, missing `secret`, and a session ran it all day and reported green.
# Flags are matched as whole tokens — `([^;&|]* )?-f` rather than `.*-f` — so a
# path like src/x-foo.py cannot trip a rule about a flag. A rule that fires on
# something legitimate gets routed around, and then it enforces nothing.
# Scoped to Bash. If a row is wrong, change it here rather than working around it.
# Two rows refused commands that change nothing, until 2026-09-23. The gate
# row matched the path after any space, so `ls -la ./scripts/gate.sh` was a
# run; it now refuses the path where the shell runs it: first on a line or in
# a command, after `(`, `{` or a backquote and a blank, or behind a keyword
# (if, do, !), a variable assignment, or a runner (bash, sh, zsh, source, .,
# env, exec, command, time, nohup, sudo, timeout N) whatever flags it is
# given, so `bash -n` and `command -v`, which only check or look the script
# up, are refused too. A runner not named here walks past, as `bash -c`
# already did, and so does `$(./scripts/gate.sh)` with no blank, as before.
# A line break or a tab reaches a row as a backslash and an `n`, `r` or `t`,
# so the start of a line is named on its own, and only unescaped: a `\n`
# typed in quoted text is two backslashes and an `n`. The staging row refused
# `git add -n -A` and `git add -A --dry-run`, which stage nothing. A regex
# cannot say "unless -n", so it refuses `git add` only when every other word
# in it is something else: a short flag holding no n, a long flag not
# starting --d, or a path. It ends at a line break as it does at a `;`.
# tool
